subject: Post-call: RAG qualification & retrieval/reranker recs for Clarity Health
messages:

Subject: Post-call: RAG qualification & retrieval/reranker recs for Clarity Health

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our call so the team has a single reference: 

Summary of needs
- Use case: clinician-facing knowledge assistant (policy + patient guidance) with strong grounding and auditability.
- Data: mix of internal docs (PDFs, Confluence) and clinical KB (structured tables). PII needs: limited; will be scoped with security.
- SLA targets: p95 generation latency < 600ms for short answers; throughput 50 qps for concurrency bursts.

Initial model & retrieval recommendations
- Model(s): Llama-3-70B-q4 (Redwood-optimized) as baseline for quality. For a low-latency pilot, propose Llama-2-Chat-13B-opt as a candidate fast path.
- Embedding: text-embedding-3-small for dense vectors.
- Retriever: HNSW index (vector store), initial top_k=10, chunk size 500 tokens, chunk overlap 64.
- Reranker: cross-encoder style reranker (we recommend our "rerank-superv-1" profile) for final ranking and grounding score.

Benchmarks & artifacts (attached/links)
- Attached: clarity_prompt_set_v1.txt (seed prompts we discussed) and perf_benchmark_clarity.csv (synthetic perf runs for 13B vs 70B).
- Drive link with eval prompts and QA pairs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-clarity-pilot-docs

Quality/regression concerns
- Primary risk: hallucination on procedural policy content where documents overlap/out-of-date. We'll instrument grounding metrics (source coverage, citation precision) and set automatic regression alerts on a held-out prompt set.
- Secondary risk: tokenization/formatting errors for tables; we recommend a table-normalization preprocessor in ingestion.

Pilot proposal & next steps
1) Confirm data connectors and sample dataset (we need a small set of representative docs and 200 seed prompts) — action: Clara to share pointer or grant Drive access.
2) Redwood to run two 3-day bench runs (13B opt vs 70B-q4) with your seed prompts, return perf + quality metrics. Deliverables: perf CSV, precision/recall on grounding, and suggested reranker thresholds. (ETA: 4 business days after data access) — action: Redwood (Lauren/Aditya).
3) Technical kickoff for pilot (30–45 min) to lock in index parameters, API keys, and telemetry hooks.

Security note
- We'll need to confirm whether you require private deployment (VPC) for the pilot or whether hosted with field-level encryption is acceptable. Attached is a short security summary (SSO_SSCQ.pdf) for procurement.

If this matches your expectations I can get the bench runs scheduled tomorrow. Happy to adjust models/configs based on your latency/cost preference.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Hi Clara — looping in a few concrete numbers and config trade-offs so your procurement/infra team has something to evaluate quickly.

Latency and reranker cost impact
- 70B-q4 (Redwood-optimized): expect median token latency + generation p50 around ~180–240ms for short answers (<= 150 tokens) on a single A100-equivalent instance; p95 is workload-dependent but we observed ~700–900ms with an aggressive cross-encoder reranker on the critical path.
- 13B-opt: median ~80–120ms; p95 ~300–450ms with the same reranker.
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker adds ~120–250ms depending on number of candidates. We typically run a lightweight bi-encoder to fetch top 30 then rerank top 8–10 with cross-encoder to balance latency and quality.

Cost (very approximate) per 10k queries (includes retrieval + generation + reranker cycles)
- 70B-q4 baseline: ~$320–420 per 10k (depends on batching and cache hit rate).
- 13B-opt baseline: ~$90–130 per 10k.

Retrieval & index tuning (recommended starting params)
- Vector store: HNSW, m=32, ef_construction=200, ef_search=512.
- Top_k retrieval: initial top_k=10 (bi-encoder), rerank top_n=8.
- Chunking: 500 token chunks with 64 token overlap; table preprocessor to flatten tables into minimal QA triples.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching on common clinician prompts (we can seed cache from your telemetry).

Quality/regression instrumentation
- We'll run the bench against your seed prompts and measure: grounding precision (fraction of answers with at least one supporting citation), source diversity, and answer calibration (confidence vs correctness) using your annotated holdout. We will configure baseline alerts for >5% drop in grounding precision vs baseline for any rollout.

Pilot path suggestion
- Start with 13B-opt for the initial 3-day bench to validate throughput and basic grounding metrics. If quality delta is significant on the prompt set we can run targeted tests on 70B-q4 for the top 200 prompts.

I attached a perf CSV from a comparable pilot we ran internally to give a sense of tradeoffs (perf_benchmark_clarity.csv). Happy to walk through numbers in the kickoff.

—Aditya
